title: Wasteland
designer: Michael A. Stackpole, Ken St. Andre, Alan Pavlish
shortDescription: Interplay's groundbreaking post-nuclear tactical RPG set in the radioactive ruins of the American Southwest, the direct creative progenitor of Fallout.
historicalSignificance: Revolutionized computer role-playing by introducing permanent persistent environmental consequences, party skills replacing strict classes, and a grim post-apocalyptic nuclear setting that directly gave birth to the legendary Fallout franchise.

editorialContent.overview: Set in 2087 following a devastating global nuclear war in 1998, players command a squad of Desert Rangers investigating a string of murders that uncovers a pre-war artificial intelligence named Cochise plotting to exterminate humanity.
editorialContent.gameplay: Pioneered multifaceted problem-solving: locked doors could be picked, blown open with TNT, or bypassed with a high strength stat. Introduced skill-based party mechanics and persistent world-state tracking.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Included a famous printed narrative 'Paragraphs Book' in the box to bypass floppy disk memory limits, directing players to read specific prose entries at narrative triggers.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Established Brian Fargo and Interplay as premier world-builders, directly serving as the spiritual father and direct mechanical predecessor to 1997's Fallout.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on 5.25-inch floppies, updated for modern PCs via Wasteland Remastered.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over 250,000 copies sold (major commercial hit for 1988)
awards: Computer Gaming World Role-Playing Game of the Year 1988
